Continue the prior research on 'Lyman-alpha forest constraints on warm/sterile DM'. Read the board, identify the two weakest claims, deepen them with a contrasting emulator/tool call and one new paper per weak claim, and post corrected findings before writing the report.

brief.summary: High-resolution Lyman-alpha forest 1D flux power spectrum (FPS) from HIRES/UVES and XQ-100 at z~4-5 provides the strongest small-scale structure probe of warm/sterile dark matter, with published thermal-relic limits m_th >5.3-5.7 keV from hydrodynamical simulations plus Bayesian/emulator inference. The signal is a scale-dependent suppression on small scales and modest enhancement on large scales in WDM vs CDM, highly degenerate with IGM thermal history (T0(z), gamma, pressure smoothing scale, mean flux, patchy reionization). Recent Gaussian-process emulators (Bird et al. LaCE, Lyssa Nyx 4096^3 120 Mpc suite, Sherwood-Relics) interpolate FPS over cosmology and IGM parameters, enabling MCMC constraints but with emulator error and prior dependence. Sterile-neutrino dark matter limits map m_th to m_s via production mechanism (Dodelson-Widrow vs resonant Shi-Fuller vs diluted), and are complemented by X-ray decay line (E=m_s/2) and BBN N_eff/Yp/D/H bounds, with mixed cold+warm models reopening keV-scale parameter space and creating tension with 0.6-1.6 keV warmness claims from other probes.

directions.goal: Use the sterile-neutrino server to compute non-resonant (Dodelson-Widrow) production: the relic abundance Omega_s h^2 and the production fraction f_s = Omega_s/Omega_dm across the (m_s, sin^2 2theta) plane. Find the mixing angle at which f_s = 1, and compare that line with the X-ray decay bounds and the Lyman-alpha DW mass floors (about 20, 22, 29 and 45 keV, from thermal-relic limits of 3.1, 3.3, 4.1 and 5.7 keV).
directions.rationale: The task explicitly asks for the sterile-nu tools to supply production fractions. The survey flagged these fractions as not yet computed, and they are the core of the comparison with non-resonant production.
steps: Call describe_sterile_nu_tools. Record the production mechanism assumed (DW or non-resonant), the validity range in m_s and sin^2 2theta, which X-ray and BBN data it uses, and whether it reports Omega_s h^2, f_s, a free-streaming scale or k_hm.
Call list_sterile_nu_skills. If a skill matches abundance or production-fraction workflows, load it with load_sterile_nu_skill and follow it.
Run predict_sterile_nu at m_s = 7.1 keV and sin^2 2theta = 7e-11 (the 3.5 keV line point) as a sanity check. Record Omega_s h^2, f_s and any reported constraints.

Run predict_sterile_nu_grid with at most 400 points. Use log-spaced m_s from 1 to 100 keV, including 20, 22, 29 and 45 keV exactly, and log-spaced sin^2 2theta from 1e-13 to 1e-6. Pass a distinct label to each call.
From the grid, extract for each mass the sin^2 2theta at which f_s = 1. Also extract f_s along the X-ray-allowed upper boundary, using predict_sterile_nu_xray_line at representative masses.
Run scan_sterile_nu_parameters over the same plane, then plot_sterile_nu_exclusion from the scan file, with output_dir set to the run directory.

Tabulate f_s at the four Lyman-alpha DW mass floors at the maximal X-ray-allowed mixing. State whether 100% DW dark matter is excluded and what fraction remains allowed. Use only numbers the tools returned.
success_criteria: A table of m_s, sin^2 2theta at which f_s = 1, the X-ray limit on sin^2 2theta, and f_s at the X-ray limit, all taken from tool output.
The exclusion plot file path as the tool reported it.
A clear statement of whether, under the tool's physics, DW sterile neutrinos at or above about 20 keV can make up all the dark matter.

result.summary:
Pure DW sterile neutrinos at 20 keV cannot be all of the dark matter under this tool's physics: the tool's own X-ray check (NuSTAR M31, Roach+ 2020) excludes the f_s = 1 point. At 29 and 45 keV the tool cannot decide either way, because it has no X-ray limit near those masses; the 'not excluded' flag there means no coverage, not allowed. The success criteria are only partly met. The f_s = 1 mixings and the plot are done, but the X-ray limit on sin^2 2theta and f_s at that limit are missing: the tool returns only an excluded/not-excluded flag from sparse tabulated points, never a numerical limit (finding f-002, question q-06). It assumes pure Dodelson-Widrow (DW) production, with Shi-Fuller resonant production as a separate option (this answers q-01). It reports Omega_s h^2, Delta N_eff, lifetime and free-streaming length, but not f_s directly and not k_hm (finding f-001).

Check at the 3.5 keV line point (7.1 keV, sin^2 2theta = 7e-11): Omega_s h^2 = 0.033, so f_s = 0.275 (tc-...-23).

Omega_s h^2 scales linearly with sin^2 2theta, which the 374-point grid confirms. At sin^2 2theta = 1e-12 the tool gives Omega_s h^2 = 0.003041 (20 keV), 0.00361 (22 keV), 0.005936 (29 keV) and 0.01309 (45 keV) (tc-...-31). Scaling to Omega_s h^2 = 0.12 gives the mixing for f_s = 1. This rescaling is my own arithmetic, not a direct tool output.

| m_s | sin^2 2theta at f_s = 1 | Tool X-ray check at that mixing |
|---|---|---|
| 20 keV | 3.95e-11 | Excluded by NuSTAR M31 (tc-...-33) |
| 22 keV | 3.32e-11 | Not run |
| 29 keV | 2.02e-11 | No tabulated limit within 30% in mass, so undecided (tc-...-35) |
| 45 keV | 9.17e-12 | No tabulated limit within 30% in mass, so undecided (tc-...-34) |
| 7.1 keV | 2.55e-10 | Not run (scaled from the same grid) |

Because there are no numerical X-ray limits, I cannot give f_s at the maximal X-ray-allowed mixing, or the fraction that remains allowed, at the four Lyman-alpha floors. This needs d-04's numerical limits: f_s,max = sin^2 2theta_X / sin^2 2theta(f_s=1).

BBN does not matter here. A 6400-point DW scan over 1-100 keV and sin^2 2theta = 1e-14 to 1e-6 found 3092 overclosing points and 968 BBN-excluded points. The largest BBN-allowed mixing is about 3e-8 near 26 keV and 1.5e-8 near 50 keV, roughly 3 orders of magnitude above the f_s = 1 line (f-003).

result.summary: Thermal-relic limits checked (f-005, tc-...-36/45/46/47). 2309.04533 (checked against the full text): m_WDM > 5.7 keV (95% CL) from HIRES+UVES at z = 4.2-5.0 with k_max = 0.2 s/km; restricting to k_max < 0.1 s/km with earlier thermal-history priors gives 4.1 keV. The other three were checked against their arXiv abstracts only, not the full texts: 2209.14220 gives > 3.1 keV with a likelihood peak at 4.5 keV (4.0 < z < 5.2, Boera+2019 data, suppression saturates at k > 0.1 s/km); 1306.2314 gives > 3.3 keV from 25 z > 4 HIRES/MIKE quasars; 1702.01764 gives XQ-100 1.4 keV, HIRES/MIKE 4.1 keV and combined 5.3 keV assuming a power-law T(z), or 3.5 keV if temperature jumps of 5000 K are allowed. Mixed-DM bounds (f-006): 2504.06367 gives f_WDM < 0.16, 0.35, 0.50, 0.67 (2 sigma) at thermal-relic masses 1, 2, 3, 4 keV (so these are thermal-relic bounds, answering q-02). 0812.0010 is expressed directly in the non-resonant (DW) sterile mass: pure-WDM limits are m_nrp >= 8 keV (99.7%) and 12.1 keV (Bayesian 95%), and any mass above 5 keV is allowed if F_wdm < 0.6 (99.7%) or F_wdm < 0.35 (Bayesian 95%). result.summary: Two of the three success criteria are not met: there is no table under a second mapping, so no spread between mappings, and the DW <p/T> check was not done. What was established: (1) The Viel et al. 2005 relation is checked against the full text (f-010; source text at /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-lyman-wdm/runs/261019_110120/astro-ph_0501562.txt). Eq. (5) reads m_sterile = 4.43 keV (m_thermal/1 keV)^{4/3} (0.25(0.7)^2/omega_x)^{1/3}, which confirms the coefficient 4.43 keV and the exponents 4/3 and -1/3. The paper gets it by equating omega_x and m_x/T_x, treating the DW spectrum as a rescaled Fermi-Dirac distribution, so the thermal and DW transfer functions are identical by construction. (2) Its fitting form is T(k) = [1+(alpha k)^{2nu}]^{-5/nu} with nu = 1.12, fitted for k < 5 h/Mpc. For thermal relics alpha = 0.049 (m_x/keV)^{-1.11} (Omega_x/0.25)^{0.11} (h/0.7)^{1.22} h^-1 Mpc. By my own arithmetic k_hm = 0.325/alpha, which gives about 23.3, 25.0, 31.8 and 45.8 h/Mpc for 3.1, 3.3, 4.1 and 5.7 keV. These lie outside the k range the fit was calibrated on, and DW k_hm is identical under this mapping (f-011). (3) My own arithmetic gives DW floors, under Viel with omega_dm = 0.12, of 20.2, 21.9, 29.3 and 45.4 keV; with omega = 0.1225 they are 20.0, 21.8, 29.1 and 45.1 keV (f-012). (4) The framework in 2007.13751 is T(k) = [1+(alpha k)^beta]^gamma. It reduces to the Viel form when beta = 2nu and gamma = -5/nu, and a 2 keV WDM is fitted by [0.02, 2.2, -4.5]. In the sections read it gives no DW-specific relation (f-013). Which mapping to use with d-01: Viel Eq. (5), because it is the convention behind the board's floors. This is a provisional recommendation: other mappings may shift the floors, but no second mapping has been checked. Not done: a second mapping (Abazajian astro-ph/0512631 was downloaded to the run directory but not read; the Bozek/Murgia half-mode relations were not found), the spread between mappings, the DW <p/T> of about 3.15 T_nu, the comparison with the tool's free-streaming length, and cite() entries in references.bib. See dead end x-03 and question q-08.

result.summary: Half the success criteria are met: the literature statements on whether pure Dodelson-Widrow (DW) production can be all of the dark matter are quote-verified, but the numerical table of X-ray limits on sin^2 2theta could not be built. (1) Literature statements, all quote-verified. Merle 2017 (arXiv:1702.08430) says DW production is 'nowadays known to be excluded by observations'; that rests on structure formation together with X-ray bounds (f-007). Roach et al. 2022 (arXiv:2207.04572, NuSTAR Milky Way halo, about 7 and 20 Ms per detector) set sin^2 2theta limits for m_s = 6-40 keV. They 'strongly disfavor a ~7-keV sterile neutrino' (the 3.5 keV line candidate) and give leading limits at about 15-18 and 25-40 keV, 'reaching or extending below the big bang nucleosynthesis limit'. They also state that the parameter space is 'mostly covered' (this includes satellite-counting bounds), but that this 'does not fully rule out sterile neutrinos as the only DM component'; only the simple mixing production mechanism 'may be insufficient' (f-008). So no source makes a clean claim that X-ray limits alone exclude 100% DW dark matter. Roach et al. 2020 (arXiv:1908.09037) give 95% limits on the decay rate Gamma (not on sin^2 2theta) for 10-40 keV, plotted in their Fig. 5 on an axis of 1e-29 to 1e-27 s^-1. They are about 2x better at 10-12 keV and weaker near 16 keV and 30-40 keV (f-009). Perez et al. 2017 (arXiv:1609.00667) give the strongest limits over most of 10-50 keV (f-004). (2) Not established: numerical sin^2 2theta limits at 7, 20, 22, 29 and 45 keV, so the X-ray-allowed f_s,max for d-01 cannot be computed yet. The papers give the limits only as figure curves, which were not digitised (dead end x-02). NuSTAR coverage ends at 40 keV, so 45 keV needs INTEGRAL/SPI or Fermi-GBM limits. (3) Files: the 2207.04572 full text is at /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-lyman-wdm/runs/261019_110120/2207.04572.txt. 2207.04572 has not yet been added to references.bib; the earlier sources 1609.00667, 1908.09037 and 1702.08430 are already cited there. Next step: run get_paper_figures on 2207.04572 (its final sin^2 2theta-versus-m_s figure) or 1908.09037 (Fig. 1, the combined plot), read the limits as approximate values, and add 2207.04572 to references.bib.

findings.claim: A DW scan of 6400 points over m_s = 1-100 keV and sin^2 2theta = 1e-14 to 1e-6 gives 3092 overclosing points (Omega_s h^2 > 0.12) and 968 BBN-excluded points. NuSTAR X-ray line searches give the leading upper limits on sin^2 2theta for keV sterile neutrinos over 10-50 keV. Perez et al. 2016 (arXiv:1609.00667, Galactic Center 0-bounce) state: "In most of the mass range 10–50 keV, these are now the strongest limits, at some masses improving upon previous limits by a factor of ∼ 10". Roach et al. 2020 (arXiv:1908.09037, Galactic bulge) find "no evidence of anomalous x-ray lines in the energy range 5–20 keV, corresponding to sterile neutrino masses 10–40 keV". In 1609.00667 Fig. 1 the limits are plotted on a sin^2 2theta axis running from 1e-15 to 1e-7; the curve values were not digitised here.

findings.claim: Cold-plus-warm bounds. Garcia-Gallego et al. 2025 (2504.06367; Sherwood-Relics with a neural-network emulator; UVES+HIRES at z = 4.2-5.0) give f_WDM < 0.16, 0.35, 0.50 and 0.67 (2 sigma) for THERMAL-RELIC masses m_WDM = 1, 2, 3 and 4 keV. Boyarsky et al. 2008 (0812.0010; WMAP5 + SDSS/VHS Lyman-alpha) state their bounds in terms of the NON-RESONANTLY PRODUCED sterile-neutrino mass. In the pure-WDM case they find m_nrp >= 8 keV (frequentist 99.7%) or 12.1 keV (Bayesian 95%). For 5 keV < m_nrp < infinity any mass is allowed when F_wdm < 0.6 (frequentist 99.7%) or F_wdm < 0.35 (Bayesian 95%).

findings.claim: Merle 2017 (arXiv:1702.08430, quote verified) says that non-resonant Dodelson-Widrow production is "nowadays known to be excluded by observations", because "the resulting spectrum would feature too many particles with rather large momenta, making this setting similar to a hot DM case and thus excluded by data". This statement rests on structure formation combined with X-ray bounds; the review does not make an X-ray-only exclusion claim.

Roach et al. 2022 (arXiv:2207.04572, NuSTAR Milky Way halo, about 7 Ms/detector blank-sky plus about 20 Ms/detector stacked data) find no anomalous lines and set sin^2(2theta) limits for m_s = 6-40 keV. Quote: "we strongly disfavor a ~7-keV sterile neutrino decaying into a 3.5-keV photon" and "we derive leading limits on sterile neutrinos with masses ~15–18 keV and ~25–40 keV, reaching or extending below the big bang nucleosynthesis limit". The conclusions add that the parameter space "is now mostly covered", but this "does not fully rule out sterile neutrinos as the only DM component"; it shows "the simple and elegant mixing production mechanism [8, 9] may be insufficient". The authors therefore do NOT claim that X-ray data alone exclude 100% DW dark matter. Their "mostly covered" statement relies on adding satellite-counting bounds.

Roach et al. 2020 (arXiv:1908.09037, NuSTAR Galactic bulge, about 190 ks) give 95% one-sided limits on the decay rate Gamma for m_s = 10-40 keV, quoted in Gamma [s^-1] rather than sin^2 2theta. Their Fig. 5 plots these limits on a Gamma axis spanning 1e-29 to 1e-27 s^-1, compared with Neronov+2016, Perez+2017 and Ng+2019. The paper states the limits are "comparable to previous NuSTAR limits" and improve on earlier ones by about 2x at 10-12 keV. They are weakened near m ~ 16 keV and 30-40 keV, where the background fit shows excesses. No numerical values were tabulated, and the curves were not digitised.

Viel et al. 2005 (astro-ph/0501562) Eq. (5), checked against the full text: m_sterile = 4.43 keV (m_thermal/1 keV)^{4/3} (0.25(0.7)^2/omega_x)^{1/3}. The coefficient 4.43 keV and the exponents 4/3 and -1/3 are confirmed, and 0.25*0.49 = 0.1225 matches the board's normalisation. The paper derives it by 'equating omega_x and m_x/T_x' of a thermal relic and a sterile neutrino 'which share the same phase-space distribution but with an overall suppression factor chi'. So it treats the DW spectrum as a rescaled Fermi-Dirac distribution with T_x = T_nu, and the two transfer functions are identical by construction.

findings.claim: The Viel 2005 transfer-function fit, checked against the full text, is T(k) = [1+(alpha k)^{2nu}]^{-5/nu} with nu = 1.12 (best fit for k < 5 h/Mpc). For thermal relics alpha = 0.049 (m_x/1 keV)^{-1.11} (Omega_x/0.25)^{0.11} (h/0.7)^{1.22} h^-1 Mpc; the general form is alpha = 0.24 ((m_x/T_x)/(1 keV/T_nu))^{-0.83} (omega_x/0.1225)^{-0.16} Mpc. The half-mode condition T^2 = 1/2 gives k_hm = (2^{nu/10}-1)^{1/(2nu)}/alpha = 0.325/alpha (my own arithmetic). Taking Omega_x = 0.25 and h = 0.7, the thermal limits give alpha = 0.01396, 0.01302, 0.01024 and 0.00710 h^-1 Mpc, so k_hm is about 23.3, 25.0, 31.8 and 45.8 h/Mpc for 3.1, 3.3, 4.1 and 5.7 keV. Under Viel's mapping the DW k_hm at the mapped mass is identical by construction.

With omega = 0.1225 exactly, the values are 20.0, 21.8, 29.1 and 45.1 keV. This confirms the board's rough figures of 20, 22, 29 and 45 keV to within 1%.

The general nCDM framework of 2007.13751 (Murgia et al. form) uses T(k) = [1+(alpha k)^beta]^gamma at z = 99, which reduces to the thermal WDM fit when beta = 2nu, gamma = -5/nu and nu = 1.12. A 2 keV WDM is fitted by [alpha, beta, gamma] = [0.02, 2.2, -4.5], with priors alpha in [0, 0.1], beta in [1, 10] and gamma in [-10, 0]. In the sections read, the paper gives no DW-specific relation between thermal-relic and sterile mass; it is applied to ultra-light axions. Using it for DW would require fitting (alpha, beta, gamma) to a Boltzmann-code DW transfer function.

findings.claim: Combined table of allowed DW fraction versus mass (Lyman-alpha side). At 7.1 keV: 0812.0010 gives F_wdm < 0.35 (quote-verified, d-02), and 2504.06367 mapped to DW mass gives f between 0.16 and 0.35 (my estimate; the mapped points are 4.4 and 11 keV). It is also below the 0812.0010 pure-DW floor of 12.1 keV, so the binding constraint is Lyman-alpha mixed-DM, f_s <~ 0.2-0.35. At 20 and 22 keV: 2504.06367 mapped gives f <~ 0.5-0.67 (mapped points 18 and 28 keV), and 20/22 keV are below the 29 keV (4.1 keV variant) and 45 keV (5.7 keV variant) Viel-mapped pure-DW floors. At 29 keV: f = 1 is allowed by Lyman-alpha only for the 4.1 keV variant (floor ~29 keV, unverified Viel mapping), while for the 5.7 keV variant f <~ 0.67 or more. At 45 keV: f = 1 is allowed by Lyman-alpha even for the 5.7 keV variant (floor ~45 keV). At 29 and 45 keV, X-ray limits are presumably binding, but no numerical X-ray limit is available, so f_s,max(X-ray) stays undetermined.

issues.text: The server is an SBBN/N_eff tool (serve-sbbn.sh), and the brief says no production-fraction tool was available. Do not assume it returns Omega_s h^2 or f_s for keV DW production. Make step 1 a go/no-go gate. If describe_sterile_nu_tools shows no DW relic-abundance output, or a validity range that excludes 1-100 keV, stop. Report the gap and do not build tables from proxies such as N_eff or BBN shifts. Write tool-derived f_s only when a tool actually returned it.

predict_sterile_nu_xray_line predicts the line energy and flux. It does not give an observational upper limit on sin^2 2theta. 'X-ray-allowed mixing' therefore needs a literature bound (see the added direction) unless describe shows the tool holds X-ray limit data. Otherwise the f_s values at the X-ray limit cannot be verified.

Step 7 is circular. The Lyman-alpha DW floors of about 20-45 keV apply only to f_s = 1. For f_s < 1, the relevant constraint is the mixed cold-plus-warm bound from d-02, converted with the mapping from d-03. Make the f_s table the comparison of tool f_s against the d-02 maximum warm fraction at each mass, and state this dependency. Also, the 7.1 keV, 7e-11 point should give f_s much less than 1 under pure DW. Treat it as a check against the expected small fraction, not as an f_s = 1 check.
Budget the grid explicitly, for example 20 masses by 20 angles = 400 points, and say what happens if one call fails. Use at most about 3 xray_line calls so the direction stays within 15 calls.

Seven papers with full-text reads, figures, a literature search and cite calls will not fit in 15 calls. Split it. (a) Limits: 2309.04533 and 2209.14220 in full, plus 1306.2314 and 1702.01764 from abstracts or metadata unless a sterile conversion is needed. (b) Mixed bounds: 0812.0010 and 2504.06367. Drop the open-ended 2023-2025 search, or cap it at a single search_arxiv_abstracts call.

Fractions read off get_paper_figures images are unverifiable. Prefer numbers quoted in the text or tables, and label any value read from a figure as approximate, with its figure number. Record whether each fraction bound is given in thermal-relic mass or in sterile mass, because 0812.0010 uses a sterile-neutrino mass.

CLASS/CAMB are not available, so the T(k)^2 half-mode-matched comparison listed under reproducible analyses cannot be computed. Limit the direction to published fitting formulas, with the arithmetic shown, and say explicitly that this is a limitation. Remove predict_sterile_nu from its tools unless d-01 confirms the tool reports k_hm or a free-streaming length. Note that the Planck value omega_dm = 0.120 changes the Viel factor by only about 0.7%. Check the coefficient as well: a quick recomputation of the formula gives 20.0, 29.1 and 45.1 keV for 3.1, 4.1 and 5.7 keV, so the brief's arithmetic is consistent and only the coefficient needs a quote.

Add at least one mapping with different exponents, such as Abazajian 2006 or a half-mode fit as used in 1702.01764 or Bozek et al. That gives a meaningful spread. Two mappings that both trace back to Viel 2005 would not.

They stop at the per-target flux lines, before any 'EXCLUDED by NuSTAR M31' or 'no tabulated limit within 30% in mass' text. tc-...-22 is only the skill-loading instructions. The exclusion verdict at 20 keV and the no-coverage verdict at 29 and 45 keV are therefore not shown in the evidence. The tool's flux model is also physically doubtful. issues.text: The tool's DW normalisation has not been cross-checked. The common Abazajian-type fit, Omega h^2 ~ 0.1 (sin^2 2theta / 3e-9)(m_s / 3 keV)^1.8, gives sin^2 2theta(f_s=1) of about 7-8e-10 at 7.1 keV. The tool's value is 2.55e-10, roughly a factor of 3 lower. DW abundance predictions differ by factors of a few in the literature (hadronic uncertainties, Asaka-Laine-Shaposhnikov). Any f_s,max derived from this line inherits that factor and must state the source of the normalisation.

The tc-...-31 excerpt shows only the 7.1 keV row. The 20, 22, 29 and 45 keV Omega_s h^2 values are not visible in the quoted evidence, although the arithmetic from them is internally consistent (0.12/0.003041 x 1e-12 = 3.95e-11, and so on). The full rows from sterile_nu_grid_DW_a74034.csv should be quoted.

The counts (968 BBN-excluded, 3092 overclosing) appear in the evidence. The maxima of the BBN-allowed mixing (3.03e-8 at 26.2 keV, 1.5e-8 at 49.7 keV) do not. Those mixings lie deep in the overclosed region, so 'BBN does not constrain DW DM' is correct but trivially so. The claim should say this.

The Merle quote attributes the DW exclusion to the hot-like momentum spectrum, which is a structure-formation argument. The finding's addition that the statement 'rests on structure formation combined with X-ray bounds' is an interpretation, not part of the quote. It should be labelled as such.

The central comparison asked by the task is still missing: f_s,max(m_s) from numerical X-ray limits, intersected with the Lyman-alpha mixed-DM bounds. q-06 and q-07 are unanswered, d-03 (the mapping) has not run, and the brief's warning that no production-fraction tool exists is stale and should be corrected.
